title: 金缕衣
author: 杜秋娘（传）
intro: Don’t treasure a robe of gold thread — treasure your youth. Pick the flower while it’s blooming, before you’re left holding a bare branch. China’s own “seize the day” poem.
analysis: 这首诗只有一个意思：珍惜青春。前两句用了两个“劝君”，一个说“莫惜”，一个说“惜取”：不要太看重用金线绣成的华丽衣服，要珍惜少年时光。衣服再贵还能再做，青春过去了就回不来了。后两句用了一个比喻：花开了，能折的时候就赶快折，不要等到花谢了，只能折一根空树枝。这首诗读起来像唱歌一样，“劝君”“惜”“折”都重复出现，朗朗上口，非常好记。“花开堪折直须折”今天还常被引用，意思是机会来了要抓住，不要等到失去了才后悔。
analysisEn: The whole poem says one thing: make the most of your youth. The first two lines both begin “I urge you” and play “don’t treasure” against “do treasure”: don’t set too much store by a splendid robe embroidered with gold thread; treasure the years when you are young. A costly robe can always be made again, but youth, once gone, never comes back. The second half turns this into a picture: when a flower is open and ready to be picked, pick it — don’t wait until the blossoms are gone and you are left snapping off an empty branch. Because the words 劝君 (“I urge you”), 惜 (“to treasure”) and 折 (“to pick, to snap off”) keep coming back, the poem sounds like a song and sticks in the memory, which is exactly what it was: a tune sung at banquets. The line about picking the flower while you can is still quoted today to mean “grab the chance while you have it, or you’ll regret it later”.
background: The poem is traditionally attributed to Du Qiuniang (c. 791–?), a talented singer who later served in the Tang palace; the poet Du Mu wrote that she used to sing it. Many scholars think it was an anonymous popular song of the time, and some editions list it as anonymous.
pronunciation: 多音字：少年 shào（年轻，不读 shǎo）；堪折 zhé。缕 lǚ。
version: 采用《唐诗三百首》通行版本，作者题杜秋娘；一说为无名氏作品，杜秋娘只是演唱者。

lines.py: quàn jūn mò xī jīn lǚ yī
lines.lit: I urge you: do not treasure the gold-threaded robe;
lines.en: Don’t set your heart on a robe of golden thread;

lines.py: quàn jūn xī qǔ shào nián shí
lines.lit: I urge you: treasure the time of youth.
lines.en: set it on the years while you are young.

lines.py: huā kāi kān zhé zhí xū zhé
lines.lit: When flowers bloom and can be picked, pick them straight away;
lines.en: When the flower is open and ready, pick it now —

lines.py: mò dài wú huā kōng zhé zhī
lines.lit: do not wait until there are no flowers and snap off an empty branch.
lines.en: don’t wait until it’s gone and break off a bare branch.

words.note: 现代汉语常用，“劝他别去”。

words.en: a robe embroidered with gold thread

words.note: 读 shào；现代汉语指十几岁的孩子，这里泛指年轻时。
古代说法，现代汉语说“就应该”。

words.en: to pick (a flower); to snap off
words.note: 现代汉语有“折断”“折一枝花”。

words.en: in vain; with nothing to show

imagery.name: 花
imagery.zh: 盛开的花比喻青春和机会，要在它最美的时候抓住。
imagery.en: The flower in bloom is youth and opportunity — seize it at its best.
